review_information.notes:
No sign-in. The app opens on the dashboard, and the bottom bar (dashboard, transfer, credit score, the Nova assistant, settings) plus the dashboard shortcuts reach every screen, including history, notifications and Borrow & Protect, which holds the loan and insurance tabs.

How data loads, which matters for review: the app calls the NexusPay backend at https://nexustransferpay.app over HTTPS, with a 4 second connect and 8 second read timeout. When a call fails or times out, the screen falls back to sample data compiled into the app so the flow still renders. The figures you are most likely to see - wallets of 4,823.42 USD, 1,284.10 EUR, 642.55 GBP and 92,450 JPY, seven recent transactions, a rising credit-score curve, the card, loan and insurance offers - are that fallback unless the backend answers. They are illustrative; they are not a real account, and no money moves in that state.

Transfer flow: enter an amount, choose the send and receive currencies, enter a recipient name (email and note optional) and confirm. The exchange rate comes from the backend and falls back to a built-in table when offline, and a reference id is shown at the end. Nothing in the reachable UI asks for a card number, bank credentials or a government ID.

The Premium screen shows monthly and annual pricing, but no billing is implemented: the button only displays a "Redirecting to payment" message, nothing is charged, and this build includes no in-app purchase product and no external purchase link. We can remove that screen if you would prefer it not ship in this state.

The binary links the system photo picker for an identity-document step that is not linked from any screen in this build, which is why a photo library usage string appears in Info.plist. There is no push-notification prompt, since Firebase is not configured here, and no advertising SDK. Theme and language are stored on the device.
